title: Hold to peek, more places to explore, and a shiny collection
body: **Hold a creature** in the battle team picker to see the moves it will bring into the fight. Let go and you are back to choosing, with nothing selected.

**More of the real world is now in play.** Tourist spots, bus stops, and industrial and service buildings all become map points, on top of the shops and amenities you already had. Parks and gardens still produce battle grunts.

**A shiny collection view.** Tap the ☆ Shiny button in your Collection to see every creature in its shiny colours. The ones you have caught shiny appear in full; the rest are silhouettes, so you can see exactly what is left to find.
**Jump straight to a family.** Open any creature in your Collection and tap "Show in your storage" to filter Storage to that whole line — every stage, pre-evolutions and evolutions included.
**This News tab.** Updates land here newest first, with a yellow dot on anything you have not read yet.

title: HUGE UPDATE! Exclusive Raids, 15 km eggs, Shiny Incense, New Missions, Move Updates and New Weekly Events
body: **Hold to multi-select.** Press and hold a creature in your Storage to start multi-select with that creature already ticked, then tap the others you want and release them together. A normal tap still opens the creature as before.

**Exclusive Raids arrive.** A new raid type appears on the map with a **blue flame** instead of the usual orange one. They hold creatures found nowhere else, and those creatures have their own Collection tab: **Exclusive**.

**Tougher bosses.** An Exclusive Raid boss has **4× HP** instead of 3×, and **+30%** Attack, Defence and Speed instead of +25%. Only rarities 3, 4 and 5 appear: **50%** rarity 3, **35%** rarity 4, **15%** rarity 5. You still catch them with an **Ultra Capture Disc**.

**New drops.** XP and stardust match a normal raid of the same rarity, and every usual raid drop still applies. On top, each win has a **25%** chance of a **Shiny Incense** and a separate **25%** chance of a **15 km egg**.

**Shiny Incense.** Works exactly like a regular Incense, except every creature you catch or hatch while it burns has a flat **3%** shiny chance. It replaces the normal odds rather than adding to them, so it does **not** stack with Shiny Bonanza. It shares the incense slot with the plain and Rare varieties.

**15 km eggs.** Only dropped by Exclusive Raids, and they only hatch Exclusive creatures — 50% rarity 3, 35% rarity 4, 15% rarity 5. They pay **+50 stardust** and **+2 candy** over a 10 km egg, and they live in **three slots of their own**, so a full set of six ordinary eggs never blocks one.

**New lifetime missions.** Seven for Exclusive Raids — one for each of rarities 3, 4 and 5, then 5, 10, 20 and 50 wins — paying XP, stardust, Ultra Capture Discs, incenses and a Stardust Magnet. Exclusive wins count towards the ordinary raid missions as well. There is also a new **Catch 7500 creatures** milestone.

**Updated point odds.** Weekdays: 22% a creature, 28% discs, 15% a potion or revive, 5% a regular raid, **2% an Exclusive Raid**, 28% nothing. Weekends: the same, but **4% an Exclusive Raid** and 26% nothing.
**Updated buff moves.** Moves that increase a creature’s stats now boost those stats by a higher percentage.

**Raid Invasion — Wednesdays 19:00–20:00.** During this hour, spinning disc POIs always give **1 ultra capture disc** on top of normal rewards. Point odds shift to: **10% creature, 40% discs, 10% potion/revive, 30% regular raid, 10% exclusive raid**.

**Training Dojo Hour — Saturdays 13:30–14:00.** Grunts take over normal POIs with **no spawn limit**. Point odds become: **10% creature, 15% discs, 35% potion/revive, 3% regular raid, 2% exclusive raid, 35% grunts**.

title: Live temperature, coordinates gone, swipe through your Collection
body: **The temperature where you are.** A new 🌡 chip sits in the top bar between your stardust and the ℹ button, showing the real outdoor temperature in **°C**. It comes from **Open-Meteo**, a free weather service, and refreshes every 15 minutes or whenever you travel a couple of kilometres. It is decoration for now — nothing in the game depends on it.

**Your coordinates are gone from the screen.** The chip under the map used to print your exact latitude and longitude, which is the last thing you want in a screenshot. The whole chip has been removed — your position is never shown as numbers anywhere in the game now. Only a location rounded to about a kilometre is sent when looking up the temperature, so the exact spot never leaves your device.

**Swipe through your Collection.** Open any creature from your Collection and swipe left or right, or use the ‹ › arrows, to move to the next one — exactly like your Storage already worked. It follows your current sort and filters, so a filtered Collection only walks the creatures that match.

**"Times caught" now sorts properly.** Sorting your Collection by Times caught was reading how many of that creature you happen to be holding, not how many you have ever caught. It now uses the **lifetime total** shown as "Total caught" on the creature's page, so releasing one no longer shuffles the order.
**New weekly mission: Walk 75 km.** Worth **75 XP**, **700 stardust** and **1 Shiny Incense**, on top of the existing 25 km and 50 km walks.

title: The Research Lab, Stat Boosters, Full Heals and Super Incubators
body: **Stat Boosters.** A brand-new item that adds a permanent **+1** to one stat of one creature — you choose which. It is applied **after everything else**, so +1 stays exactly +1 no matter how much that creature levels up or evolves. Tap one in your Items, pick a creature, then pick HP, Attack, Defence or Speed; you see the stat as it is now and what it becomes before you confirm. Each creature can hold **20 boosts in total** across all four stats, so spending 8 on Attack and 12 on Defence finishes it.

**The Research Lab.** A new building, pinned to the map once just like a Breeding Centre. Visit it and choose **Create items** to turn spare candy into Stat Boosters. The price depends on the rarity of the family whose candy you spend: **Common 50**, **Uncommon 30**, **Rare 15**, **Epic and Legendary 10** candy per booster. Pick a family, set how many with − and +, and confirm. Boosters are **not tied to the candy that made them** — spend Common candy and use the booster on your Legendary if you like.

**How to get the lab.** A new lifetime mission: **Reach level 7 and register 70 creatures**, paying **50 XP**, **200 stardust**, **1 Incense** and **1 Research Lab**. Stat Boosters also turn up from grunt battles at **10%**, so you can start before the lab arrives.

**Full Heal.** Takes one creature straight back to full HP however badly hurt it is, instead of feeding it potions 50 HP at a time. It cannot revive a fainted creature — that still needs a Revive. **Every grunt win** gives one, and a potion or revive point carries one **10%** of the time. In the battle team picker you now get both options: **Heal all** spends potions, **Full Heal** spends these, worst hurt first, so you decide which to burn.

**Super Incubator.** Works like a Single Use Incubator but cuts the distance the egg needs by **25%** — a 10 km egg hatches after 7.5 km, a 5 km after 3.75 km, a 15 km after 11.25 km. Dropped by grunt battles at **30%**, and by a couple of daily missions.
**Single Use Incubators are rarer from raids.** Rarity 1 to 3 raid wins now drop one **20%** of the time instead of 50%. Rarity 4 and 5 bosses still hand one over **guaranteed**.

**See your creatures properly.** Tap the picture on any creature's page, in Storage or in your Collection, to open it full screen. It shows whichever art you are looking at, so shiny toggles carry through.

title: Galactic Adventures: 77 new creatures, a Set missions tab, and the first Mythical
body: **A second creature set: Galactic Adventures.** 77 brand-new creatures, with their own Collection tab sitting between Elemental Awakening and Exclusive. They are **locked to begin with** — you open them one rarity at a time.

**A new Missions tab: Set.** Five missions, and they never reset. Each one wants a number of **Elemental Awakening** creatures registered *and* an amount of total XP, and claiming it puts that rarity of Galactic Adventures into circulation for good: **65 registered + 10,000 XP** opens rarity 1, **70 + 13,000 XP** rarity 2, **75 + 18,000 XP** rarity 3, **77 + 22,000 XP** rarity 4, and **all 79 + 25,000 XP** rarity 5. The bar fills as you register; the Claim button waits for the XP.
**Nothing happens until you claim.** Completing the mission is not enough — the rarity opens on the claim.

**Once open, they are everywhere.** Wild spawns, incense, eggs, raids and grunt teams all draw from the same pool, so grunts will start bringing **mixed teams** from both sets. The odds have not changed: a wild spawn is still 60% rarity 1, 28% rarity 2, 8% rarity 3, 3% rarity 4, 1% rarity 5. There are simply more creatures in each tier to pick from.

**The last rung pays big.** Register all 79 Elemental Awakening creatures with 25,000 total XP and you get **150 XP**, **1,500 stardust**, rarity 5 Galactic Adventures, **1 Breeding Centre** and a **50 km egg**.

**Mythicals — rarity 6.** A new tier above Legendary, with its own Collection tab. Mythicals never spawn, never appear in a raid and never hatch from an ordinary egg. Each has one specific way of being found.

**Astralyon, the first Mythical.** The 50 km egg holds it, guaranteed — no roll, and nothing else will ever come out of that egg. It hatches at **level 3** with **500 stardust** and **25 candy**. It **cannot** hatch shiny, and the egg **ignores your storage limits**, so it lands even with every other egg slot full.

**Multi-stat buff moves.** A Mythical's buff move raises **several stats at once** instead of one. Astralyon's **Extreme Growth** lifts Attack, Defence and Speed together by 15% each, and the battle log names every stat it touched.

**Mythical rates.** A Mythical buddy earns one candy every **20 km** — the longest walk in the game. Catching one is worth **30 XP** and **5 candy**, a Stat Booster from Mythical candy costs **10**, and a Mythical pair in the Breeding Centre takes **48 hours** per candy. You can also filter your Collection by **6 · Mythical**.
**Coming soon got an update too.** More Mythicals are on the way, and work has started on the set after Galactic Adventures — filling in a set is what opens the next one.

title: The Shop is open: watch a video, earn coins, spend them on supplies
body: **A new Shop tab.** Sitting between Missions and News, it trades a new currency — 🪙 **coins** — for the consumables you get through fastest.

**Earning coins.** Tap **Watch a video** and you get **1 coin** per video watched. There is no limit on how many you watch, and coins **never expire**, so an unspent one is still waiting tomorrow. Nothing starts on its own — you always choose to watch.

**What's on the shelves.** **2 Capturing Discs** for 1 coin (up to 3 a day) · **2 Potions** for 1 coin (up to 5) · **2 Revives** for 1 coin (up to 5) · **1 Ultra Capture Disc** for 1 coin (up to 2) · **1 Single Use Incubator** for 2 coins (up to 1) · **1 Incense** for 3 coins (up to 1) · **1 Stardust Magnet** for 3 coins (up to 1).

**The limits are daily, per item.** Each row shows how many you have left for today, and they all reset at **midnight** local time, the same moment your daily missions do. Buying every row to its limit costs 🪙 23, so that is the most a single day's watching can be worth.

**Nothing is locked behind it.** Every item the Shop sells still drops from map points, raids, grunts and missions exactly as before. The Shop is a shortcut when you have run dry mid-walk, not a gate.

title: Creature Spotlight, Essence Harvesting, the Molten Seeker, and buildings you can move
body: **Creature Spotlight — Mondays 18:00 to 19:00.** One creature takes over the map for the hour, and it rotates every week. Tap **📅 Calendar** in the News tab to see who is next.

**How the spotlight changes spawns.** During the hour, any wild or incense spawn that draws the featured creature's **rarity** has a **50%** chance of being that creature instead of a normal pick from the tier. Draw a different rarity and nothing changes at all — the rarity odds themselves never move, only which rarity-N creature you meet.

**It also comes to you.** The featured creature appears right on your position on a fixed schedule, guaranteed, and waits **5 minutes**. How often depends on its rarity: a **Common** turns up at 18:00, 18:10, 18:20, 18:30, 18:40 and 18:50; an **Uncommon** every 15 minutes; **Rare** and **Epic** every 20; a **Legendary** at 18:00 and 18:30.
**And it pays more.** Catching the featured creature during its hour gives **+2 candy**. Anything else you catch is unaffected. Eggs and raids are left alone.

**Essence Harvesting — a new way to get candy.** From **player level 2**, once you have registered anything, a creature you already know leaves an **essence** somewhere in your 250 m scan radius. It shows as that creature's own picture on the map and lasts **30 minutes**. One appears per **2-hour block** — midnight to 2am, 2 to 4, and so on — the first time you open the game during it.

**The mini-game.** Tap the essence and the creature drifts around inside three rings. Tap the rings to draw the essence out: **3 candy** for the bullseye, **2** for the middle ring, **1** for the outer one, nothing for a miss. No disc, no capture, and you can play it from **any distance**.

**Distance decides your pins.** A pin is one tap. Over **200 m** away gets you 1, **150–200 m** 2, **100–150 m** 3, **50–100 m** 4, **25–50 m** 5, and **within 25 m** a full 6. Rarer creatures have tighter rings and drift faster, so a Legendary is a genuine test.

**Molten Seeker.** A new item, and a **15%** reward whenever a harvest pays you at least one candy. Using one widens your reach from **25 m to 50 m for 15 minutes** — creatures, discs, raids, grunts and your buildings all become tappable from twice as far. It has its own effect slot, so it runs alongside an incense and a Stardust Magnet.

**New missions for it.** Lifetime: get candy from Essence Harvesting **10** times (10 XP, 50 dust), **20** (20 XP, 75), **50** (30 XP, 150, 1 Single Use Incubator), **100** (50 XP, 250, 1 Super Incubator) and **250** (80 XP, 500, 1 Molten Seeker, 1 Rare Incense). Daily: **3** times (10 XP, 75 dust, 1 Ultra Capture Disc). Weekly: **20** times (20 XP, 150 dust, 1 Molten Seeker). Only harvests that actually paid candy count.

**Set missions now run on XP, not level.** The Galactic Adventures ladder asks for total XP instead of a player level: **65 registered + 10,000 XP**, **70 + 13,000**, **75 + 18,000**, **77 + 22,000**, and **all 79 + 25,000**. The row tells you how much XP you still need.

**Your breeding centre tells you when candy is ready.** A gold pip appears on the map pin the moment any slot hits its 5-candy cap, with a number on it if more than one is waiting. The slot is highlighted and marked FULL inside the sheet too.

**Buildings can be moved.** Both the Breeding Centre and the Research Lab now have a **Move** button that puts them back in your Items so you can pin them somewhere better. The centre needs every pair collected first — creatures left inside would have nowhere to come back to.

title: Creature abilities are here
body: **Some creatures now have an ability.** An ability is a permanent trait that makes a creature hit harder, or hold up better, whenever a particular condition is true — and does nothing at all when it is not. **16 creatures** have one to begin with, and more will follow.

**Where to find them.** The Collection has a new **Ability** filter: set it to **✦ Has an ability** to see exactly who has one. Open any creature and tap the **✦ button** under its picture to read what its ability does and what sets it off.

**What can set one off.** The opposing creature's **type**, **stage**, **rarity** or **set**; the **temperature**, **cloud cover**, **humidity** or **wind** where you are; the **time** of day, the **day** of the week, the **month** — and new in this update, **daylight**, meaning whether the sun is up where you are. One ability can hold several conditions at once, sometimes pulling in opposite directions.

**Shadowflit and Flutterwing — Night Owl.** They deal **50% more** damage at night, and take **50% more** in daylight. Day or night comes from the same weather reading the HUD chip shows, so it follows real sunrise and sunset rather than a fixed clock.

**A few of the others.** **Toxiforge** deals 40% more against Mechanic creatures. **Mystikeon** deals 40% more against rarity 4 and 5. **Notreclast** takes 40% less from Stage 1. **Gelibara** deals 40% more in December, January and February, and takes 40% more in July, August and September. **Brasquente** deals 50% more at 25°C or above and 50% less below 5°C. **Beanknight** deals 40% more at weekends.

**The team picker tells you which ones will actually help.** While you are choosing a team for a raid or a grunt battle, each tile now carries a marker: a lit **✦** means that creature's ability **will** apply in this battle, a hollow **✧** means it has one that **will not**, and no marker means it has none. Tap and hold still previews its moves as before.

**Sort by it.** The picker's sort list has a new **Ability in this battle** option that brings the creatures whose abilities fire to the front. It already knows who you are about to fight — the boss for a raid, all three creatures for a grunt — as well as the weather and the clock, so the answer is the real one rather than a guess. When an ability only fires against part of a grunt's team, the marker says so when you hold on it.

**In the fight.** Abilities announce themselves as creatures take the field and again whenever a new opponent steps up, and the log says whether one **triggered** or **not triggered**, along with the reason. If several conditions fire at once their effects multiply, and the total is capped between **0.25×** and **4×**, so no stack can trivialise a battle.
**One thing worth knowing.** The weather-based ones need a weather reading to work from. With no reading they simply do not fire — the game never guesses at the conditions.

title: Held items: give your creatures something to carry
body: **A new Held items tab** sits in your Storage, next to Creatures, Items and Eggs. A creature can carry **one held item** at a time, and most items only suit part of your roster — some are locked to a **type**, some to a **stage**, some to a **level**.

**Two ways to hand one over.** Tap an item in the new tab and you get every creature that can hold it, with the exact stat change it would make. Or open a creature and use its **Held item** slot to see your spares, with the ones that do not suit it greyed out and the reason why. Taking an item back off is one tap — except for the consumables, which cannot come back.

**Gems, Shields and Cogs.** One of each per type, and only a creature of that type can hold it. A **Gem** gives **+10 Attack**, a **Shield** **+10 Defence**, a **Cog** **+10 Speed**. The figure is added after level growth, so +10 is worth exactly +10 at level 1 and at level 10.

**Miracle Coin.** If an attack would knock the holder out **from full health**, it survives on **1 HP** instead. Once it has taken any damage at all it can be knocked out in one hit like anything else, so it rewards going into a fight fresh.
**Growth Crystal.** **+20 HP**, for a **Stage 2** creature only. Evolve that creature to Stage 3 and the crystal comes straight back to your storage rather than being wasted.
**Strength Sigil.** **+20 Attack** for a creature at **level 8 or above**.

**Breeding Amulet — consumable.** Put two creatures that are **both** holding one into the Breeding Centre and their candy arrives **twice as fast**. One amulet on its own does nothing. Both are used up once that pair has earned its full **5 candy**; collect them early and the amulets survive for another go.

**Candy Pouch — consumable.** While the holder is your **buddy** it needs **half the usual distance** to earn a candy. The pouch is spent the moment it earns one, so it is worth saving for a rarer buddy with a longer walk.

**Where they come from.** Beat a **raid** and there is a chance of one, depending on the boss's level: **1%** at level 3 or 4, **2%** at level 5 or 6, **4%** at level 7 or 8. When one drops there is a **40%** chance it is one of the two consumables and **60%** it is one of the others.
**And one a week, guaranteed.** A new weekly mission — **Log in to the game this week** — pays a **random held item** on top of 10 XP and 50 stardust. Opening the game completes it.

**In battle.** A creature carrying something says so as it takes the field, and the log names the item. If a Miracle Coin saves one, the log says what the hit would have been and that it was left on 1 HP.

**Training Dojo Hour, corrected.** During the hour grunts still take over shops, amenities and the other ordinary map points with **no limit** on how many of those appear. **Parks and gardens are no longer part of it**: they roll as they always do, scattered across your scan radius and capped at 6 between them. Previously the event lifted that cap too, which filled the map with grunts standing nowhere near a point.

**Your save now has a cloud backup.** Once a day, in the background, your progress is copied to a private cloud record. It is a safety net for a lost or wiped phone — the save in your browser, and the save file you can link in Profile, are still the ones the game actually uses. Nothing to set up and nothing to log into.

title: Watch an ad for a coin, and Full Heals join the Exchange corner
body: **Watch an ad.** The Shop's earn button is now **Watch an ad**. Tap it and a small panel offers you a link; open the link and the advert appears in a **separate tab**, with your 🪙 coin paid the moment you open it. Your game stays exactly where it was, so you can come straight back. Still one coin an ad, still no daily limit on earning, and nothing ever starts on its own.

**A Full Heal from a win is now a coin flip.** Raid wins and grunt wins each carry a **Full Heal 50%** of the time instead of every time. Nothing else about those rewards changed: a raid win still always pays **2 Revives**, a grunt win still always pays healing supplies, and a potion or revive point still carries a Full Heal **10%** of the time.

**Full Heals now trade at the Exchange corner**, at exactly the same rate as Potions in both directions. **6 Full Heals** buys 2 Potions, 2 Revives, 2 Capturing Discs, 1 Ultra Capture Disc or 1 Single Use Incubator — and every other deal now offers Full Heals back, so 6 Potions, 6 Revives or 6 Capturing Discs each buy **2 Full Heals**, as do 3 Ultra Capture Discs or 3 Single Use Incubators.

title: Sweet Toothsday, a Galactic takeover, two new items, and the climb to level 20
body: **Sweet Toothsday.** Every **Tuesday, all day**, candy from **catching** a creature, **catching a raid boss** and **hatching an egg** is **doubled**. Bonuses double too, so a raid catch's +2 and an egg's bonus candy both count, and the reward screen tells you it landed. Buddy walking, the breeding centre, Essence Harvesting and releasing are unchanged — those pay by distance or by the clock, and doubling them would reward a walk you started on Monday.

**Galactic Adventures Take Over.** Every **Thursday 18:00–19:00**, once you have opened at least one rarity of Galactic Adventures, the whole map changes hands: wild spawns, incense spawns, ordinary raid bosses and 5 and 10 km egg hatches all come from your **unlocked Galactic creatures**, and the Elemental Awakening pool sits the hour out entirely. The **odds are untouched** — a rarity 1 roll is still a rarity 1 roll, it just picks from a different list. Exclusive Raids and the 15 km and 50 km eggs are left alone, since they are the only route to those creatures.

**Never lose an essence again.** When a creature leaves an essence, a **flickering rainbow arrow** now points straight at it and stays on screen however far you zoom in or pan away. Off screen, it pins itself to the edge of the view, still aimed the right way, with the distance you would have to walk. **Tap the arrow** to open the harvest from wherever you are. It only disappears once you have played the mini game — or when the essence runs out.

**New item: Mysterious Incense.** The one incense you get to aim. Pick any **Stage 1** creature you have **registered** and every single spawn is that creature, one every 2 minutes lasting 1 min 30 s, exactly like a plain Incense. The trade is time, set by the rarity you choose: **Common 30 min · Uncommon 20 min · Rare 12 min · Epic 8 min · Legendary 4 min**. Exclusive and Mythical creatures are never on the list. It drops from **grunt** wins (**1%**) and **raid** wins — **1%** for a rarity 1 or 2 boss, **2%** rarity 3, **3%** rarity 4, **4%** rarity 5.

**New item: Strength Re-roll Stone.** Draws one creature's **stat modifier** again — the stat that is 10% up and the stat that is 10% down. The new pair is **guaranteed to be different** on both counts: whatever was going up will not be going up, and whatever was going down will not be going down. You cannot choose what it becomes, so it is a way out of a bad roll rather than a route to a perfect creature. A creature on full HP stays on full even if its maximum moves.

**The level cap is now 20.** Levels 16 to 20 each pay everything level 15 did **plus a Molten Seeker, a Shiny Incense, a Mysterious Incense and a Strength Re-roll Stone** — every level, not just once. The XP steps grow by about 20% each time: **24,000** more for level 16, then 29,000, 35,000, 42,000 and **50,000**. Level 20 sits at **260,000 XP** in total.

title: The last two creature levels hit harder, and a tidier Held items tab
body: **Levels 9 and 10 are worth more now.** Each of those two levels adds **20%** of the base stat instead of 10%, across **all four stats** — HP, Attack, Defence and Speed. It is still measured against the base stat, so a level 10 creature sits at **×2.1** its base figures rather than ×1.9, and the extra is not compounded on top of level 9. Levels 1 to 8 are completely unchanged, and every creature you already own picked this up the moment it loaded — including a little more maximum HP.

**The Held items tab shows one grid at a time.** Free items and the ones already out on creatures used to be stacked on the same page, which on a phone left a second grid buried under the first. There is now a single toggle at the top: it opens on **Free**, tap it for **Being held**, tap again to go back. Each view reads like the Items grid next door, and the tab remembers which one you were last looking at.

title: A lot more of your street is now on the map
body: **New map points.** Six more kinds of real place now become points: **trees**, **poles** of both the street-furniture and electricity varieties, **pedestrian crossings**, and every **leisure** spot that is not a park or a garden — pitches, playgrounds, sports centres, nature reserves. They roll exactly the same odds as a shop or a bus stop, so a quiet residential street is no longer an empty map.
**Nothing gets crowded out.** Points still keep **15 m** from each other, so a road lined with twenty trees produces only what fits rather than twenty spawns in a row.

**Grass is now grunt territory.** Areas tagged as **grass** join parks and gardens as places battle grunts appear, at the same quieter **25%** rate as a garden — a park is still the busiest at **40%**.

**And more grunts can be out at once.** The ceiling across all green space has gone from **6 to 11**, so the new grass areas add grunts to find rather than competing for the same six slots. Each area still rolls 3 times, grunts still keep 20 m apart, and the once-per-8-hours trainer who walks up to you still does not use a slot.

title: A tighter map that refreshes twice as often
body: **Scans now cover 150 m instead of 250 m, and run every 1 min 30 s instead of every 3 minutes.** All those new point types made a 250 m circle very busy in town — busy enough that the map itself started to feel heavy. A smaller circle refreshed more often turns out to be better on both counts: less to draw at once, and never long to wait for something new. In quiet areas you lose very little, because the new point types more than made up for the smaller radius.

**Trees are out.** `natural=tree` was the densest source by far and the main reason city maps got sluggish. Everything else added recently stays: poles, pedestrian crossings, and leisure spots like pitches, playgrounds and sports centres.

**Essence Harvesting pins have been rebalanced** for the smaller radius, so the pin bands still span the whole area you can be from one: **over 125 m** 1 pin · **100–125 m** 2 · **75–100 m** 3 · **50–75 m** 4 · **25–50 m** 5 · **within 25 m** 6. In practice essences now turn up closer, so most harvests give you more pins than before.

**Grunts come to you a bit more.** Park, garden and grass grunts scatter across the scan radius, so they now appear within 150 m rather than 250 m — the same 11 of them in a smaller area, which means less walking between fights.

title: 25 more Exclusive creatures, and moves that do more than damage
body: **A new Set mission: register 19 Exclusive creatures.** It pays 50 XP and 500 stardust, and it opens a **second wave of 25 Exclusive creatures**. They join the same **Exclusive** collection tab and the same Exclusive Raid and 15 km egg pools — but only once you have claimed it. Until then they are not in the Collection at all, so filling in the first 19 is the whole job. There is no XP gate on this one: getting 19 raid-only creatures registered is quite enough.

**Moves can now do more than hit.** A move may **heal the creature using it** by a set number of HP, **raise its own** Attack, Defence or Speed, **lower the opponent's**, or **lower its own** as the price of a heavy swing. These ride on top of the damage where a move has any — so a move can hit for 20 and heal 40 on the same turn — and the battle log gives each part its own line and its own colour.

**A stat can go down as well as up.** A lowered stat lasts the rest of the fight unless something raises it again, and buffs and debuffs cancel each other out on the same stat. Nothing can be ground below 1, so a pile of debuffs never leaves a creature doing literally nothing.

**The breeding pair Confirm button now follows you.** It sticks to the bottom of the picker like the battle team's fight button, so with a storage full of creatures you no longer have to scroll all the way down to confirm a pair. The "pick two of the same creature" warning moved down with it, so the reason the button is greyed out is right next to the button.

title: Place as many breeding centres as you like, and a Buildings list to fetch them back
body: **More than one breeding centre.** You can now pin as many as you own, and **each one has its own full set of slots** — your player level sets how many slots a centre has, so a second centre doubles how many pairs you can have breeding at once.

**A Buildings list in your Items.** Breeding Centres and the Research Lab have moved out of the ordinary item grid into a **Buildings** card of their own. Open it and you see everything: the ones spare in your bag and every one already on the map, wherever it is.

**And you can always fetch one back.** Any placed building can be brought home from that list. Previously a breeding centre could only be picked up by standing next to it and only if it was empty — so pinning one somewhere you never went back to meant losing it, and with it breeding, for good. Bringing a centre back frees any pairs inside, but **any candy they have earned and not been collected for is lost**, and the game says exactly how much before you confirm. Collect them at the centre first if you want to keep it.
**Three more things in the Shop.** **Rare Incense** for 10 coins, and **Shiny Incense** and **Mysterious Incense** for 50 each. One of each per day.
**A shorter chip for the Galactic takeover.** It now shows just the event name and the time left — the full description did not fit on a phone.

title: Temporal Rift: 74 new creatures, evolutions you choose, and creatures that only appear sometimes
body: **A third creature set: Temporal Rift.** 74 brand-new creatures, with their own Collection tab sitting straight after Galactic Adventures. Like that set they are **locked to begin with**, and they open one rarity at a time — but this ladder is climbed off the back of **Galactic Adventures** rather than the first set.

**Five new Set missions.** Each wants a number of **Galactic Adventures** creatures registered *and* an amount of total XP: **65 registered + 24,000 XP** opens rarity 1, **70 + 27,000** rarity 2, **73 + 30,000** rarity 3, **75 + 33,000** rarity 4, and **all 77 + 38,000** rarity 5. As always the bar fills as you register and the Claim button waits for the XP, and nothing enters circulation until you actually claim.

**The last rung pays a new Mythical.** All 77 Galactic Adventures creatures with 38,000 total XP gives you **175 XP**, **1,750 stardust**, rarity 5 Temporal Rift, a **Mysterious Incense** and a **Chromarion 50 km egg**.

**Chromarion, the second Mythical.** Rarity 6, Mechanic, and it comes from an egg of its very own — Astralyon's 50 km egg is untouched, so a second Mythical cannot dilute the first. Its **Extreme Failure** is the mirror of Astralyon's buff: it drops the opponent's **Attack, Defence and Speed together** by 15% each. Like Astralyon's egg it never rolls shiny and ignores your storage limits.

**Some creatures now have more than one possible evolution.** A handful of Temporal Rift creatures can grow into **several different creatures**, and **you choose which**. Tap Evolve and it asks first, showing each option with its type and its stat total. **Vulpetta** has the widest fork in the game with four ways to go; **Funglet** has two.

**The choice is permanent, but not exclusive.** It costs the same candy whichever branch you take, and every branch shares **one candy pool** and **one family** — so candy you already saved works for any of them, and nothing stops you raising a second one and taking a different path. Because the game cannot know which way you will go, a creature that forks lists only its own moves rather than promising the ones further along.

**And some creatures only appear under certain conditions.** **12** of them wait for something before they will spawn on the map, lead a raid or hatch from an egg — and outside that window they are simply not in the pool at all.

**What they are waiting for.** **Mythloon** only comes out at **night** and **Solflare** only in **daylight**. **Umbropplet** needs **rain actually falling**, **Nimbearis** over **80% cloud**, **Craggit** over **75% humidity**, **Cycloblaze** over **18°C** and **Harpuddle** under **10°C**. **Snoozoth** appears on **Mondays**, **Sanctuarch** on **Sundays**, and **Desklerk** keeps office hours — **weekdays, 9am to 5pm**.

**Two of them want something from you.** **Anukibi** turns up once you have walked more than **2 km today**, and **Gridlet** once you have beaten more than **2 grunts today**. Both reset with your daily missions at midnight.

**You can always see how close you are.** Open one of these in your Collection and it lists exactly what it needs, with the **current reading beside each line** — so "needs over 18°C" is answered by "it is 14°C" rather than left a mystery, and the panel turns green when it is worth going out to look. The weather ones need a **weather reading** to work from; without one they stay away, because the game never guesses at the conditions.

**A condition only decides whether one can turn up.** Catch it once and it is yours for good — it battles, levels and evolves whenever you like, and it keeps its place in your Collection. A **Mysterious Incense** will only offer you one while its condition is currently met, but once lit it keeps summoning for the full burn.

**Moves can now raise the opponent's stats.** Not a bug — a **drawback**, and it is what pays for an unusually heavy hit. **Faygoal Wind's Wind Goal** swings for 65 and hands the opponent **30% more Attack**; **Florvulpa's Last Recovery** swings for 79 and gives it **25% more Speed**. The battle log names whose stats moved, so a buff landing on the wrong side of the field is never a surprise.

**Coming soon: a fourth set, and biomes.** Where you walk is about to matter as much as when. Creatures will belong to **particular parts of the world** — some only in cities, some only next to water, others out in open countryside.

title: 36 new abilities, and a lot more the game can notice about you
body: **Abilities have gone from 16 creatures to 52.** Open your **Collection**, set the **Ability** filter to **✦ Has an ability**, and tap the ✦ button on anyone to read what theirs does. The new ones lean much less on the weather and much more on how you actually play.

**Your day now counts.** **Long Strider** (Pigmoat) hits 30% harder once you have walked 5 km today and **Massive Strider** (Gearstrike) 40% harder past 7 km. **Raid Veteran** (Steelspirit) wants 5 raids won today, **Street Brawler** (Mummira) 5 grunts beaten, and **Lucky Star** (Quirkquack) just one shiny caught. **Master Collector** (Zenethra) is the big one: catch 50 creatures in a day and it deals **50% more** and takes **50% less**. All of these reset at midnight with your daily missions.

**So does where you are standing.** **Mountaineer** (Antaray) takes 50% less damage above 250 m and **Elevated Tantrum** (Zenquaza) deals 30% more above 150 m, while **Ocean Levelled** (Mousucklord) wants you at 100 m or below. The elevation comes from the same weather reading the 🌡 chip already uses, so it costs nothing extra and nothing new is sent.

**And how built up it is.** **Busy Roads** (Snickurl) rewards a town — 20 or more points found by your last scan — and **Country Roads** (Fluffbill) rewards a quiet lane, at 7 or fewer. It is the same count the map is built from, so it follows you as you walk.

**Even your battery.** **Fully Charged** (Aerobloom) deals 30% more at 80% charge or above; **Last Breath** (Blossomgale) deals 30% more at 20% or below. One thing to know: **iPhones and Firefox do not let a website read the battery at all**, so those two abilities can never trigger there. Everything else in this update works the same everywhere.

**Abilities that read the fight itself.** **Second Wind** (Lizaflora) takes 30% less damage at 60% HP or below and **Desperate Fury** (Sunbloss) deals 25% more below 30%. **First Strike** (Rosalia) deals 30% more against something still on full HP. **Last Stand** (Comiscroaker) deals 45% more when it is the only one left, and **Blowing Rainbow** (Prismarine) is the reverse — steadier while it has team mates, more fragile once it is alone.

**Abilities that watch your opponent.** **Tiny Terror** (Voltveil) deals 25% more against level 8 and up, **Underdog** (Earloam) takes 25% less from them. **Thief's Instinct** (Aegiscelis) deals 20% more against anything carrying a **held item**. **Armour Breaker** (Nimbearis) takes 40% less from an opponent that has **raised its own Defence** — so setting up against it backfires.

**Perfect Formation — abilities that need the right team.** **Breezebuzz** and **Zephyrbuzz** each deal **100% more** and take **50% less** while the other one is on the team. **Flakette**, **Canelette** and **Rollinette** do the same, but all three have to be there. It keeps working after a team mate has fainted: what matters is who you brought.

**Parting Shot — hitting back on the way down.** **Traphex** and **Saltstormi** take **30% of whatever the creature that beat them had left** as they are knocked out. Against something healthy that is a serious dent; against something nearly finished it will take it down with it. It can win you a fight you had already lost.

**Moonlit Frenzy** (Photosynthra) deals 45% more on a **full moon**, worked out from the date, and **Pay Day** (Serafina) deals 30% more from the **25th of the month** onwards. **Fresh Start** (Strutalon) covers the first five days instead.

**Also new: Ultra Resistance** (Frostant) takes 30% less from Mystic, Wind *and* Mechanic, **Rain Immunity** (Goggly) takes 75% less above 70% humidity, and **Smoothie Season** now belongs to **Ectomango** as well as Orbitmelon.

**The team picker has a third badge.** ✦ still means the ability **will** apply and ✧ that it **will not**, but abilities that depend on how the fight unfolds — HP, who is left standing, being knocked out — now show **✧?** instead of a confident no. Sorting by **Ability in this battle** puts ✦ first, then ✧?.

**One rule has not changed.** Anything that needs a reading — the weather, the elevation, the battery, how built up it is — **does not fire until there is one**. The game never guesses at the conditions.

title: Nine events for the year: Easter eggs, a Halloween haul, and a creature every hour
body: **Nine annual events now sit on the calendar**, each lasting three days apart from the Holiday Season. Tap **📅 Calendar** in the News tab to see what is coming, and a green chip appears on the map whenever one is running.

**Most of them bring you a creature every hour.** It turns up **on your own position** at the top of each clock hour and waits **30 minutes** — one per hour, and opening the game late in an hour still gets you that hour's creature. The odds are the point: **15% Common, 20% Uncommon, 30% Rare, 20% Epic, 15% Legendary**, which makes a Legendary fifteen times more likely than from an ordinary spawn.

**🐣 Easter Egg Hunt — Good Friday to Easter Sunday.** Any egg you put into an incubator during those three days needs **half the distance**, on top of whatever the incubator already saves: a **5 km egg** in a plain Incubator hatches at **2.5 km**, and a **15 km egg** in a Super Incubator at **5.625 km**. The discount belongs to the egg rather than the day, so a long egg started on Easter Sunday keeps it right through to hatching — the tile shows a 🐣½ badge so you can see which of your eggs are carrying it. Every hatch during the event also pays **+3 candy and +20 stardust**.
**🎃 Halloween — 29 to 31 October.** Every **catch**, **raid catch** and **hatch** pays **+3 candy**, and the hourly creature is drawn from a hand-picked cast rather than a type.
**🦃 Thanksgiving — the Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday** of the week of the fourth Thursday in November, so it moves each year. Its hourly creature has its own hand-picked cast.

**🎁 Holiday Season — 20 December to 1 January**, the longest event of the year. Every catch, raid catch and hatch pays **+1 candy and +15 stardust**; the hourly creature can be **anything you could normally catch**; and a new daily mission, **Log in today**, hands over a **random held item** plus **one incense** — 45% an ordinary Incense, 30% Rare, 15% Shiny, 10% Mysterious. The mission only exists during the event, so it will not sit in your list the rest of the year.

**Five awareness days, one type each.** **🔧 Labour Day** (1–3 May) brings **Mechanic**. **🌱 World Environment Day** (5–7 June) brings **Celestial**. **🐦 World Seabird Day** (3–5 July) brings **Wind**. **🕊 World Humanitarian Day** (19–21 August) brings **Mystic**. **☮ International Day of Peace** (21–23 September) brings **Neutral**.

**Event bonuses stack with the weekly ones.** They are added before the multipliers, so Halloween's +3 candy on a **Sweet Toothsday** is worth 6, and the Holiday +15 stardust on a **Stardust Sunday** is worth 30.

**Event creatures play by the usual rules otherwise.** They never include **Exclusives** or **Mythicals**, they only draw from sets you have unlocked, and they still respect a creature's **spawn conditions** — an event cannot conjure something the weather says is not around.

title: The Find box now filters as well as searches
body: **Your storage search takes filters.** Typing a name works exactly as it did, but the box now also understands what you are actually looking for. There is a **?** beside it listing everything it takes.
**`type = celestial`** narrows to one type — any of the five. **`type = mystic, wind`** takes several, and **`type != neutral`** excludes instead.
**`level > 4`** filters by level, and **`=`, `<`, `>=` and `<=`** all work. Two terms make a range: `level >= 3 & level <= 6`.

**`speed > 120`** filters by a stat — **HP, Attack, Defence or Speed**. It uses the figure on the creature's own page, so its level growth, its ±10% roll, any **Stat Boosters** and whatever it is **holding** are all counted. What you see on the sheet is what the filter matches. Defence can be spelled either way.

**`buff = attack`** finds every creature whose **+10%** roll landed on Attack, and **`debuff = speed`** every one that took the **−10%** on Speed. Put them together — `buff = attack & debuff = speed` — to find the ones rolled exactly how you want them.
**Join anything with `&` and all of it has to hold.** `type = mystic & attack > 70` is every Mystic you own hitting above 70. A name can be one of the terms too, so `toxi & level > 5` works.
**Two more that came along for free:** `rarity = 5` and `stage = 2`.

**It tells you when you get it wrong.** Mistype a filter — `type = dragon`, `speed > abc` — and the bar says so and suggests what it expected, rather than quietly showing you an empty grid. The chip above the results also echoes back how your query was read, so there is never any doubt what is being filtered.
**Whole family** still widens a **name** to its whole evolution line, but it greys out for a query that is only filters — `level > 8` has no line to widen to.

title: Where you caught it, purple incense spawns, and a lot of small fixes
body: **Every creature now remembers where it came from.** Open one in your Storage and the bottom of its page reads **"Caught on 30 August 2026 in Manchester, United Kingdom"**. Hatched creatures say hatched. Your position is rounded to about a kilometre before the place name is looked up — the same rounding the temperature already uses — so the exact spot never leaves your device, and if the lookup does not answer you simply get the date. Creatures you already own keep their date and have no place, since it was not being recorded before.

**Incense spawns are purple, and you can reach them from anywhere.** You paid an item to summon a creature to yourself, so having to walk the last few metres to it was a poor reward. They are now tappable at any distance — like Essence Harvesting — and the stars are purple rather than turning green when you get close, because there is no longer a "close" for them to turn on.

**The item pickers have the Storage toolbar.** Using a **Stat Booster**, a Potion, a Revive or a Strength Re-roll Stone now gives you the same **Find box and sort** as your Storage tab — including the whole filter language, so `type = mystic & level > 5` works there too. It keeps its own settings, so hunting for something to boost does not rearrange the tab you were last on.

**Buildings on the map use their real artwork.** The Breeding Centre and Research Lab show their actual item icons instead of a flag and a microscope, so the pin and the card in your Items are recognisably the same thing. They also **no longer bob** — a building is a fixed landmark, and with several on screen the movement made the map feel restless. They still glow green when you are close enough to use them.

**Your shiny Collection now remembers whole families.** Evolve a shiny Stage 1 into a Stage 2 and then a Stage 3, and **all three** show as obtained even though you only hold the last one. Existing saves are corrected on load: a Stage 2 or 3 creature can only ever be reached by evolving, so holding a shiny final form proves you once had the earlier ones.

**Unregistered creatures no longer give themselves away.** Tapping the greyed-out picture in the Collection used to open the real artwork full screen. It now refuses and tells you to register the creature first. The same applies in **shiny mode**: the sheet opens on the shiny artwork to match the grid you tapped it from, shows a silhouette if you have never obtained that shiny, and will not zoom it until you have.

**Incense and Stardust Magnet drops have been halved.** Rare Incense from a rarity 4 or 5 raid is now **12.5%** (was 25%), Shiny Incense from an Exclusive Raid **12.5%** (was 25%), and a Mysterious Incense from a grunt **0.5%** (was 1%) or from a raid **0.5% to 2%** depending on the boss. A grunt win now carries a **2.5%** chance of an Incense and **2.5%** of a Stardust Magnet, each down from 5%. Nothing changed about the incenses you get from levelling, missions or the Shop.
**A lowered stat now reads properly in battle.** It used to show as **"Speed +-50%"**; it now shows **"Speed -50%"**, and the pill is red rather than the green one used for a buff.

**The team picker's hold preview shows abilities.** Press and hold a creature while choosing a team and it now names its **ability** and describes it, underneath the moves, along with whether it will apply in this battle.

title: The Battle Frontier: five challenges, ten levels, fifteen ways through
body: **A new building: the Battle Frontier.** Pin it to the map like a Breeding Centre and there is a trainer waiting inside at every level of every challenge. Nothing here runs on a timer, so it is the one place you can battle whenever you feel like it.
**How to get it.** A new lifetime mission: **Reach level 9 and register 100 creatures**, paying **100 XP**, **300 stardust**, **1 Rare Incense** and **1 Battle Frontier**.

**Five challenges, one per type.** Mystic, Celestial, Neutral, Wind and Mechanic, each with its own trainer. Every creature they bring is that challenge's type, so you know the matchup before you walk in.

**Ten levels, fought in order.** Level 1 is three level 3 creatures with modest stats. By level 10 it is three level 9 creatures with over 320 total base stats, all **20 Stat Booster points** spent and all holding an item — as strong as a team you could field yourself. Held items and boosts start appearing at level 6 and grow from there.

**Modes are the real difficulty.** A mode restricts what **you** may bring, and there are **15**: one for each type, one for each rarity, one for each of Elemental Awakening, Galactic Adventures and Temporal Rift, **Only Exclusives**, and **No restriction**. The team picker shows only the creatures that qualify and tells you how many that is.

**A level counts as beaten once per mode.** Clear level 1 on No restriction and you can clear it again on Only Rarity 3 for the reward a second time — but never twice on the same mode. That is 150 fights per challenge if you want them all.

**Every win pays.** Levels 1 to 10 give **1 Potion, 1 Full Heal, 2 Revives, 1 Ultra Capture Disc and 1 Molten Seeker**. From **level 4** add a **random held item**, from **level 6** a **Stat Booster**, and from **level 8** a **Strength Re-roll Stone** and a **Mysterious Incense**.

**The Grand Raid Challenge.** Clear all ten levels on one mode and a level 11 in all but name opens up: a **level 8** boss with full **Exclusive Raid** strength, fought under the **same restriction** on your team. Win and you catch it with an **Ultra Capture Disc** on the usual raid shiny odds.

**Five bosses that exist nowhere else.** **Necrosmion** guards the Mystic ladder, **Yerba** the Celestial, **Aprorok** the Neutral, **Origamiros** the Wind and **Terravoltz** the Mechanic. Each is **rarity 5** with **370 total base stats**, and each joins your **Exclusive** collection at the bottom of the tab. No raid, no egg and no incense anywhere in the game can produce one. A challenge always has the **same boss on every mode**, so clearing the same ladder under a different restriction is another chance to catch it — and it can come out shiny on the usual raid odds.
**Move it freely.** Your progress lives in your save rather than in the building, so **Move Battle Frontier** re-pins it anywhere without costing you a single clear.
**Buildings list tidied up.** The Buildings sheet now shows each building's own artwork rather than a glyph, and knows which ones you are only allowed one of.
